title: Science built by Filipinos, for Filipinos: RSTW 2026 opens August 6 in Valenzuela City - DOST-NCR
text: Science built by Filipinos, for Filipinos: RSTW 2026 opens August 6 in Valenzuela City Filipino ideas, technologies, and success stories will take center stage as the Department of Science and Technology–National Capital Region (DOST-NCR), together with the City of Valenzuela, hosts the 2026 Regional Science, Technology, and Innovation Week (RSTW), its flagship celebration of homegrown science and innovation, from August 6–8, 2026, in Valenzuela City. This year’s celebration carries the theme “Siyensya, Teknolohiya at Inobasyon: Kabalikat sa Matatag, Maginhawa at Panatag na Kinabukasan,” with the sub-theme “Science, Technology, and Digital Innovation Driving Food Security, Sustainable Energy, and National Resilience.” While science is often associated with complex concepts, technical jargon, and even mathematical models and equations, its purpose is ultimately simple: to solve real problems and improve people’s lives. Through RSTW, the public is invited to discover, experience, and appreciate these innovations firsthand—bringing science closer to every Filipino. Technology You Can See in Action Visitors will get an up-close look at Filipino-developed technologies that are already creating real impact in communities and businesses. Discover how the PAGASA National Hydro-Met Observing Network (PANaHON) provides near real-time weather updates that help communities prepare for changing weather conditions. Learn how Filipino MSMEs are embracing smarter operations through the DOST-CUATRO program and the Advanced Manufacturing Center, which support businesses in adopting modern technologies and improving productivity. For a more immersive experience, visitors can also try VirtuHalal, a virtual reality training platform developed by FEU Institute of Technology and TESDA that strengthens skills and supports the growing Halal industry in the NCR. These are just some of the many technologies yet to be discovered at the 2026 RSTW. Conversations for a Better Metro Manila Following its sub-theme, the three-day event promises a rich learning experience through a series of forums and knowledge-sharing sessions. Highlights include the PhilAASTI Luzon Island Seminar, Ani at Huli sa Nagbabagong Klima: Mga Perspektiba sa Kalakhang Maynila, and TEKNOLOKAL: Bridging Technology Commercialization and Adoption for Food Security, Sustainable Energy, and National Resilience, alongside many other discussions on emerging science, technology, and innovation topics. These sessions will bring together experts, innovators, government agencies, and communities to exchange ideas, share best practices, and inspire collaborative, science-based solutions for a more resilient future. Together, these forums offer multiple entry points into the conversation, whichever angle visitors are most curious about. Innovators Solving Urban Problems Youngsters can also test their skills against their peers through several competitions that have been lined up throughout the three-day fair: Grade 6 students can unleash their artistic prowess through the ‘Blue Horizons: Sci-Art Poster Making Competition’; high school and college students who are into gaming can join the ‘Gear Up NCR: Esports Game Dev Challenge’; and college students and professionals can channel their creativity for a cause through the ‘Code Green: Digital Solution Hackathon for a Circular Economy’. Aside from these, participants can also satisfy their food cravings with the products to be sold at the bazaar, featuring products from the Small Enterprise Technology Upgrading Program, Community Empowerment thru Science and Technology, and Innovations for Filipinos Working Distantly from the Philippines beneficiaries. More than a science event, RSTW 2026 is a reminder that science isn’t meant to stay in laboratories or textbooks, but to be felt in the everyday lives of Filipinos—in the food on their table, the power in their homes, and the safety of their communities. It is an invitation for every Filipino, regardless of background or profession, to see that science and innovation are not reserved for a few but are solutions and opportunities for all. Because, as DOST’s catchy song goes, “Science is for Everyone, Science is for Everybody.” Join us on August 6–8, 2026, in Valenzuela City, and discover how science, technology, and innovation are being built—from the Filipinos, for the Filipinos. To pre-register, visit the official microsite of the event through this link: https://rstw2026.dostncr.ph/ By Aurora F. Marcelo and Maji Manel B. Medenilla

title: Start-Up QC Student Competition - Quezon City Government
text: The Quezon City Government, through the QC Local Economic Development and Investment Promotions Office (QC LEDIPO), has extended its Start-Up program to students from various schools and universities in the city, encouraging them to join and pitch their innovative business proposals that will help the city’s key sectors, such as agriculture, finance, education, health, information technology, culture, and arts. As part of the program, every batch, referred to as “Squad,” receives training, mentorship, and networking activities facilitated by the local government to nurture the entrepreneurial spirit among students and inspire them to develop their ideas. Qualified participants who have submitted their business plans have the chance to win the following cash prizes: First Place – P100,000.00 Second Place – P75,000.00 Third Place – P50,000.00 Gold Winners – P35,000.00 Silver Winners – P25,000.00 Bronze Winners – P15,000.00 With the QC Start-Up program for students, the city government aims to foster economic growth by empowering youth-led innovation and entrepreneurship, helping address significant societal challenges, and potentially creating job opportunities in the future. As of April 2026, the program has completed Squad 1 with 27 student awardees and Squad 2 with 29. The program has also opened the competition for Squad 3. Along with the QC Start-up program for professionals and businesses, this initiative is part of Mayor Joy Belmonte’s 14-point agenda, which aims to foster an environment conducive to businesses and startups while also promoting the development of innovative products, systems, and processes. To know more about the program, kindly reach out to QC LEDIPO or check out the FAQ: Start-Up QC. Interested applicants may visit the official Start-Up Facebook page and follow the QC Gov FB page for city-wide announcements and updates. For the list of student awardees from SQUAD 1 and 2, please refer to the list below. title: WPU IDEA Pitch 2026 Champions Youth Innovation and Agripreneurship - Western Philippines University
text: Western Philippines University (WPU) showcased the ingenuity of its student innovators during the WPU IDEA Pitch: Innovation, Development, Enterprise, and Agribusiness Pitch Competition 2026 held on July 22 at the WPU Training Center, Main Campus. With the theme “Empowering Youth Agripreneurs through Agristart-up Pitching,” the competition challenged students to transform innovative ideas into viable and sustainable agribusiness ventures. Eight finalist teams pitched their business concepts before a panel of judges, demonstrating creativity, market viability, and entrepreneurial potential. Below is the list of winners: - Champion: High-Protein Cassava Chips – Third-Year BS Agribusiness, WPU Main Campus - Second Place: Project Ubeyond – Fourth-Year BS Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering - Third Place: Crunch Mix – First-Year BS Agribusiness, WPU Main Campus - Special Award: Better Bite Bitter (BBB) – BS Agribusiness, WPU Quezon Campus Organized by the Agribusiness Department of the College of Agriculture, Forestry and Environmental Sciences (CAFES), headed by Mr. Eduardo E. Lleve and the Agribusiness Students Association, the event was conducted in partnership with the Department of Agriculture–Young Farmers Challenge Program MIMAROPA. The competition reaffirmed WPU’s commitment to nurturing innovation, entrepreneurship, and enterprise development among students, empowering the next generation of agripreneurs to create sustainable solutions for the agriculture sector.

title: Polytechnic University of the Philippines
text: ASEAN AI Hackathon 2026 Brings Together Innovators for Collaborative Solutions Gicel Roger Salvilla, News, Communication Management Office SDG 4 SDG 9 SDG 11 SDG 16 SDG 17 The PUP Research Institute for Strategic Foresight and Innovation (RISFI), hosted its segment of the ASEAN AI Hackathon 2026, an initiative that convened student innovators, academic leaders, and partner institutions under the theme “AI for a Resilient ASEAN: Innovation, Sustainability, and Humanity.” Photo courtesy of: PUP Research Institute for Strategic Foresight and Innovation 'Official' Facebook Page The event served as a strategic platform for knowledge exchange and collaboration across Southeast Asia, reinforcing the shared vision of developing responsible and future-ready AI solutions. It gathered key members of the technical committee, including Dr. James Ronald O. Mesina (Mapúa Malayan Colleges Laguna), PUP Vice President for Research, Extension, and Development, Dr. Anna Ruby P. Gapasin, and Assoc. Prof. Nguyen Gia Nhu (Duy Tan University), highlighting strong inter-institutional partnerships. Dr. Hang Le, Director of the P2A Secretariat and Vice Provost of Duy Tan University, emphasized the importance of regional cooperation in advancing AI innovation. This direction was reinforced by keynote speakers Dr. Ethel Valenzuela, Chair of the ASEAN AI Council, and Prof. Duong Quang Trung, President of the ASEAN Research Network, who underscored the role of artificial intelligence in promoting resilience, sustainability, and inclusive growth across ASEAN nations. Photo courtesy of: PUP Research Institute for Strategic Foresight and Innovation 'Official' Facebook Page A central component of the PUP-hosted activities was the Technical Architecture and Data Ethics Workshop, facilitated by PUP experts Dr. Robert G. de Luna, Engr. Marife A. Rosales, Engr. Orland D. Tubola, and Engr. Tristan L. Velardo. The session focused on responsible AI development, ethical data use, and sustainable technological practices—key considerations in the evolving digital landscape. Photo courtesy of: PUP Research Institute for Strategic Foresight and Innovation 'Official' Facebook Page Dr. Anna Ruby P. Gapasin, who emphasized the need to sustain academic collaborations and innovation-driven initiatives to ensure a resilient ASEAN. The event recorded significant engagement, with 1,080+ student participants, 240+ registered projects, 100+ institutions, and representation from nine ASEAN countries, reflecting the scale and impact of the initiative. Aligned with global development priorities, the ASEAN AI Hackathon 2026 contributes to several United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The initiative supports SDG 4 (Quality Education) by enhancing competencies in artificial intelligence and innovation; SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure) through the promotion of research and technological advancement; and SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities) by encouraging AI-driven solutions to societal challenges. It also upholds SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions) through its emphasis on data ethics and responsible AI, and SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals) by strengthening regional cooperation among ASEAN institutions. Through this initiative, the University continues to contribute to the advancement of a collaborative, innovative, and sustainable ASEAN community.

title: QCU Hosts PIIE–NSC NCR Qualifying Rounds 2026, Showcases Excellence in Industrial Engineering – Quezon City University
text: QCU Hosts PIIE–NSC NCR Qualifying Rounds 2026, Showcases Excellence in Industrial Engineering Quezon City University (QCU), through the PIIE-ORSP QCU Student Chapter, successfully hosted the PIIE–NSC NCR Qualifying Rounds 2026 on April 11, 2026. Organized by the Philippine Institute of Industrial Engineers – National Student Chapter (PIIE-NSC), the event gathered top Industrial Engineering students from leading higher education institutions across the National Capital Region, including De La Salle University–Manila, University of the Philippines–Diliman, Colegio de Muntinlupa, Adamson University, Polytechnic University of the Philippines–Manila, Mapúa University, Colegio de San Juan de Letran–Manila, New Era University, Technological Institute of the Philippines–Manila and Quezon City, and Quezon City University. The competition featured a series of academic and skills-based events, including the Case Study Hackathon, Feasibility Study Competition, and Inter-University Quiz Bee. These activities provided participants with a dynamic platform to showcase their analytical thinking, problem-solving abilities, and teamwork—core competencies essential in the field of industrial engineering. The opening program was formally welcomed by QCU President Dr. Theresita V. Atienza, who highlighted the value of academic collaboration and the pursuit of excellence among aspiring industrial engineers. In the Inter-University Quiz Bee, QCU was represented by Jorous John M. Lopez, Chesca Mae M. Casiquin, Desiree Jane Maramara, and Laura Isabel D. Tolentino, under the guidance of their coach, Engr. Raniel B. Taripe. The team delivered a commendable performance, securing 5th place among competing institutions. Meanwhile, the QCU Feasibility Study team—composed of Mark Al Jhun Español, Lorentz Hendrik Goloyugo, Atasha Nicole Macabale, and Princes Narvasa—was mentored by Dr. Nina Apusaga, demonstrating strong research and project development capabilities. The successful hosting of the PIIE–NSC NCR Qualifying Rounds 2026 highlights Quezon City University’s commitment to fostering academic excellence, nurturing student potential, and strengthening industry-relevant skills. Through initiatives like this, QCU continues to empower future industrial engineers to become innovative, competent, and globally competitive professionals. #1QCU #QCURISE #QCUWeRISEtogether

title: CIT students secure top spots in HackForGov 5 regional competition | Don Mariano Marcos Memorial State University
text: Students from the College of Information Technology (CIT) bagged top awards during the HackForGov 5 – Region 1 cybersecurity competition held in Bantay, Ilocos Sur, on August 19, 2026. Guided by coach Edelvar A. Malamion, students Jan Jeffrie Salloman, Mawel Aban, Achilles Rex Flores, and Miggell Tippi Tobias of the MLUC tr0jans secured 2nd Runner-Up in the regional contest. The team excelled in complex technical challenges, including web exploitation, digital forensics, OSINT, network analysis, and steganography. A second delegation, MLUC tr0jans 2.0, took 7th place overall. The group comprised Lance Renielle Apigo, Princess Janary Balagot, Earl Louie Sobremonte, and Christian Jay Rimando. Among them were those who also earned high individual rankings in the event. Princess Janary Balagot finished in the Top 6, while Miggell Tippi Tobias and Mawel Aban placed in the Top 8 and Top 10, respectively. (By Dennis Pangilinan)

title: NASA Space Apps Challenge
text: In partnership with JOIN NASA SPACE APPS CHALLENGE NOVEMBER 14-15, 2026 The NASA Space Apps Challenge offers opportunities for anyone with an interest in space and science to address real-world challenges through our annual hackathon and global community. All ages, skill levels, and professional backgrounds are welcome. At NASA Space Apps, there's always space for one more! Real-World Challenges The annual NASA Space Apps Challenge provides the opportunity to engage directly with NASA’s data, along with Space Agency Partner data. During the two-day hackathon, teams use this data to address challenges written by NASA Subject Matter Experts, featuring topics including storytelling, software development, astrophysics, space exploration, agriculture, and more. “I believe it is paramount to give the next generation of scientists, engineers, designers, and more from across the world a chance to contribute to NASA’s overall mission. The NASA Space Apps Challenge provides this opportunity by giving people – from all backgrounds and walks of life – a way to engage directly with NASA scientists and open data,” said Dr. Nicky Fox, Associate Administrator for NASA’s Science Mission Directorate. Meet like-minded individuals When you participate in NASA Space Apps, you join a community that shares a desire to propel humanity forward through scientific and technological innovation. “The NASA Space Apps Challenge changed my perspective on NASA’s data. I realized there are so many different datasets, and we can use them to make solutions that matter here on Earth or even in space.” - Space Apps Participant 2025 NASA Space Apps Challenge Global Winners Each year, thousands of teams submit projects that demonstrate collaboration, creativity, and address challenges we face on Earth and in space using NASA data. These projects undergo multiple rounds of judging to determine the 10 Global Winners, representing the most innovative projects submitted by participants. text: Legal & Privacy Terms Operated by ThinkStartup ThinkStartup Learning Private Limited · youthideathon.in · Effective July 2026 This is one page. Everything lives here — use the links below to jump to a section. Written in plain language so students and parents can actually read it. Contents 1. Most participants are under 18, so we also explain how we handle children’s data. What we collect - From the student: full name, class, school name, city, state, email, WhatsApp number, and a password. - From the parent / guardian: name, phone number, and email. - Your idea: the idea details you submit to the competition. - Site usage: a small set of named events only — for example, which registration steps you completed or clicks on our own buttons. We do not record your screen or run behavioural tracking on logged-in students (see Cookies & Analytics). Why we collect it each purpose is separate We use your information only for the purpose it was given for. We do not quietly reuse it for something else. - (a) To run the competition — register you, verify your entry, judge ideas, issue certificates, and contact you about your participation. - (b) To send competition updates — deadlines, results and event news, by WhatsApp, email or SMS. - (c) To keep your parent / guardian informed about your participation. - (d) To tell your parent / guardian about ThinkStartup’s learning products and courses — only if the optional offers box was ticked at registration. You can opt out at any time. A note on marketing We send occasional updates and offers about our learning products and courses only to people who have agreed to receive them — a parent / guardian who ticked the offers box, or an adult student who opted in. Students under 18 receive service messages only (confirmations, reminders and results), not marketing. Every marketing message carries a one-tap opt-out. The consent behind this You give consent when you register, by ticking the box: “I agree to the Terms & Conditions and Privacy Policy.” That consent is specific to the purposes above and can be withdrawn at any time. For students under 18, we also message the parent / guardian so they can object or withdraw — more in the Terms & Conditions. Who we share it with We share your information only with named categories of partners, and only for the purpose each is named for: - Evaluators / judges who score the ideas. - Logistics & shipping partners who deliver prizes to winners. - Messaging providers who send our WhatsApp, email and SMS on our behalf. - Analytics providers who help us understand site usage (see Cookies & Analytics). We do not sell your data, and we do not hand it to unnamed “third parties” for their own marketing. Your rights, and how to use them - Access a copy of the information we hold about you. - Correct anything that’s wrong. - Erase your information. - Withdraw consent — and this is as easy as giving it (one click, or reply STOP to any message). To use any of these, contact our Grievance Officer in the Contact section. How long we keep it We keep your information only as long as we need it to run the competition and meet legal duties. We delete or anonymise it within 1 year of the season ending, unless the law requires us to keep something longer. Children’s data Youth Ideathon is for students, and many are under 18. We collect a parent / guardian’s contact so we can notify them and so they can object or withdraw at any time. We do not run behavioural advertising, profiling, or tracking directed at children, and we do not send marketing or product offers to students under 18 — any offers go to a consenting parent / guardian. Security & changes We use reasonable safeguards to protect your information and store passwords securely; no system is ever 100% secure. If we change this policy we’ll post the new version here with an updated effective date. These Terms govern your use of youthideathon.in and your participation in Youth Ideathon. By registering, you agree to these Terms and to the Privacy Policy above. Who can take part Youth Ideathon is open to students in classes 8–12 and to UG / PG students. If you are under 18, a parent or guardian must be looped in at registration (see Consent below). title: UNESCO Youth Hackathon 2026 | UNESCO
text: Event UNESCO Youth Hackathon 2026 The record-breaking 2025 edition, which attracted over 1,200 teams from 138 countries, demonstrated the power of young people to drive innovation and create impactful solutions for today’s rapidly evolving information environment. Building in this momentum, the UNESCO Youth Hackathon 2026, under the theme of "Play Your Part: Youth Designing the Future of Media and Information Literacy", recognizes young people as key drivers of innovation and change, empowering them to contribute their creativity, leadership, and diverse perspectives to advance Media and Information Literacy (MIL) worldwide. The winning teams will be invited by UNESCO to participate in the Voices European Festival of Journalism and Media Freedom in Thessaloniki, Greece, from 26–28 November 2026, where they will have the opportunity to showcase their projects and engage with other stakeholders. Mentoring Programme All registered participants will have access to a two-day mentoring programme scheduled for 1 - 2 July featuring experts in Media and Information Literacy (MIL), digital transformation, artificial intelligence, project development, and innovation. These sessions are designed to help you strengthen your ideas and prepare a competitive project proposal. PS: Live session places are limited and will be allocated on a first-come, first-served basis, so early registration is highly recommended. Participants who do not secure a live place will still receive full access to recordings and learning materials. How to Prepare Tips for your preparation Who Can Participate UNESCO invites young changemakers to join this global event: - Teams of 2–6 members (national, regional, or international) - All team members must be 18–30 years old - Teams should align with UNESCO’s values, including peace, respect for diversity, and freedom of expression - Gender balance and inclusion are highly encouraged - No prior experience required—only passion and motivation! Where to Start? Teams can choose one or more of the following focus areas: - AI and MIL: Innovative solutions addressing challenges posed by AI through MIL - MIL Education: Creative approaches to MIL learning in the digital age - Community Impact: MIL-based interventions that empower communities - Youth Engagement: Strategies to position youth organizations as MIL change agents - Open Track: Other MIL-related ideas aligned with this year’s theme What Kind of Proposals Are We Looking For? Your proposal can be one of the following categories: - Games - Applications/Websites - Radio programmes/Podcasts - Artistic work such as comics, short videos, documentaries, etc. - Educational toolkits - Youth organization campaigns - Community-based interventions - Other creative modalities for innovative interventions How to Submit? Each team must prepare two components, which can be submitted in English. Proposal Document (PDF or Word format, size limit: 10MB ) - Include team members, problem statement, objectives, target audience, prototype or concept, sustainability, creativity, and feasibility - Keep it clear, concise, well-structured and readable Pitch Video (max. 3 minutes) Create a short video that showcases your project idea in a clear and engaging way. This is your chance to bring your concept to life and convince the jury of its value. - Tell the story behind your idea: What problem are you solving, and why does it matter? - Explain your solution: What is your project? How does it work? Who will benefit from it? - Highlight originality and impact: What makes your idea unique or meaningful? What kind of impact it would have? How to Select the Winners A group of international experts will review all projects during 18 August to 13 September. Each project will be reviewed by 3 experts, to ensure a fair process, based on the criteria below: - Consistency with the Theme：strong alignment with this year's theme and MIL principles - Clarity of Presentation：clear communication, strong skills, diversity, and potential to deliver - Innovation & Creativity：fresh, original, or inventive approach - Feasibility & Sustainability：realistic, resource-aware, long-term potential - Impact & Inclusion：addresses a real problem, promotes social good, meets the needs of diverse/marginalized communities What Can Winners Receive? Four winning teams will be selected at the mid of September. The winning teams will be invited to Voice Festival in Thessaloniki, Greece from November 26-28. UNESCO will cover 2 members of each team for their flight, accommdation and meal to Greece. Therefore, you are able to change your team formation when you do the submission. title: 50+ Hackathon Project Ideas 2026: Beginner to Advanced
text: - How can participating in hackathons help you? - Types of hackathons - 25+ Best Hackathon Ideas - Some popular hackathons - Tips to win a hackathon 50+ Trending Hackathon Project Ideas for Students: Beginner to Advanced Hackathons are coding competitions or sprints where programmers/developers compete against each other to solve a problem statement with the perfect code. Here are some tips, tricks, and amazing hackathon project ideas to ace these events. A hackathon is a fast-paced tech event where coders, developers, and innovators, both beginners and pros, come together to solve real-world problems through creative software or hardware solutions. Participants work in teams to build functional prototypes, typically within a tight time frame of 24 to 48 hours. While often hosted by tech companies or universities, hackathons can be organized by anyone with a passion for innovation. The goal is to spark fresh ideas, explore innovative technologies, and collaborate under pressure. For organizers, hackathons offer not only new product concepts but also a chance to spot talent and build dynamic tech communities. In this article, we’ve curated a list of beginner-to-advanced hackathon ideas, whether you are looking to build your first project, explore AI and automation, tackle a Smart India Hackathon-style problem statement, or simply learn by doing. These ideas are designed to help you get started with confidence and creativity. How can participating in hackathons help you? Hackathons are a great opportunity for learning about advanced concepts of programming. You get exposure to industry practices and understand how things work behind the scenes. Learning things practically, especially when you are studying gives you a lot of experience and helps you to master important and beneficial skills. You get to learn what innovative solutions the industry requires and how you should supply them. This will give you the much-needed confidence as a working professional in the industry. Besides, participating in hackathons will also help you to master things that will make you employable in the future. With the right hackathon ideas, you, as an IT professional, can use this chance to show your skills and highlight that you could be a valuable worker for the company if you get the right platform to prove yourself. Types of hackathons Hackathons are intensive, time-bound events where developers, designers, and innovators come together to build solutions, typically in the form of software or hardware projects. Depending on their focus and purpose, hackathons can be classified in multiple ways. Two major classification frameworks are: - By the organizing body - By the theme or technical focus Let’s explore both categories in detail: 1. Based on Organizing Body These can further be classified into: Private Hackathons These are organized by independent groups, universities, or communities. The goal may vary - from encouraging innovation to networking or community learning. Private hackathons often have a broad theme and attract a diverse set of participants, especially students or freelancers. Corporate Hackathons Organized by companies or startups, corporate hackathons are often internal (for employees) or external (for the public or targeted professionals). These are designed to solve business-specific problems, identify talent, or drive innovation within a company’s domain. They may also be part of a company’s hiring or R&D strategy. These hackathons often double as an employer branding exercise, helping companies showcase their culture and tech stack to potential hires. If your organization wants to host a branded hackathon, Unstop’s platform manages the entire process, from registration to evaluation. 2. Based on Theme or Technical Focus Application-Based Hackathons In these hackathons, participants are required to develop a complete software application or prototype. The problem statement may ask them to build something from scratch - like a mobile app, web tool, or product, or improve an existing solution. The focus is on usability, functionality, and innovation in app development. Example: - Build a smart budgeting app for college students - Add accessibility features to an existing education platform Programming Language / API / Framework-Based Hackathons Here, the emphasis is not on what is being built, but on how it’s being built. Participants are asked to work with a specific programming language (like Python or JavaScript), API (like Google Maps API, OpenAI API), or framework (like React or Django). Creativity and technical mastery in using that technology are the key judging criteria. Example: - Build anything using the OpenAI API - Create a tool using only HTML/CSS and Vanilla JavaScript - Use TensorFlow to create a machine learning project These classifications help participants understand the expectations and tailor their efforts accordingly.
